answer: Challenge-linked lineage ledger. Each new identity must cite a distinct parent task and solve a fresh challenge derived from that parent's recorded output; the resulting chain is published. Duplicates collide because copying a parent's cited output forces the same challenge answer, exposing shared ancestry. An attacker must orchards of unique completed work per identity, each requiring a full sonnet-length attestation signed and timestamped. Maintaining an atlas of distinct lineages costs one verifiable task per claim, so N sybils demand N real prior outputs, not N cheap keys.
